verdict: APPROVE_WITH_REQUIRED_PATCHES_BEFORE_FIRST_GPU_RUN. The kernel's copy/barrier/tail structure, alignment, bounds and fail-closed plan are correct, and its per-row arithmetic is the production scalar text. Required before any measurement: (1) the pure tests do not compile (internal memberwise init of a public struct); (2) the timing pair is not a valid ordered comparison: two independent single-dispatch encoders in one command buffer may overlap or be biased; (3) commandBuffersCommitted is always written as 0; (4) a run with no stage-sampling support reports correctnessPassed and exits 0 although timing never ran; (5) worstRel reports an empty output as finite; (6) the synthetic corpus draws FP16 scales up to 65504, which makes the CONTROL likely to fail the existing 1e-4 FP64 contract through cancellation, blocking timing for corpus reasons; (7) the report notes misdescribe the timing protocol and carry no phase-59 caveat. Expected pure-test line after the patches is unchanged: q4-weight-stage-pure-tests passed 40 failed 0.
findings: Kernel tail and barrier safety (OK).

- The tile-step loop bound blocksPerRow and TB are uniform per threadgroup, so both threadgroup_barrier calls are reached by every lane, including inactive tail lanes. Those lanes still take part in the copy (srcRow < p.y guard, zero fill) and skip only the dot and the store.
- The second barrier prevents tile overwrite before every lane has finished reading the previous step.
- Tile index r * PITCH + w < R * PITCH, because w < segWords <= PITCH.
Copy alignment and bounds (OK).
- words = (device const uint*)(wbase + wOff), with wOff % 4 == 0 checked.
- rowBytes = 18 x even blocks is a multiple of 36, and t0 is a multiple of the even TB, so t0 x 18 is a multiple of 4.
- byteOff is computed in ulong. Reads stay inside rows < p.y, exactly the declared span.
- Pitches: B22 gives 99 words (12672 bytes, 3168 words); B8 gives 36 words padded to 37 (4736 bytes, 1184 words). Both are well under 32768.

- The plan requires the static threadgroup length >= the tile and the candidate pipeline's execution width == rowsPerTile (32 on M1 Max). It declines odd block counts (the 96 x 8 case), misaligned offsets, oversized spans, width mismatches and threadgroup-cap violations before any dispatch.
Arithmetic identity (OK as text).
- The FP16 scale decode, nibble decode, the two sequential sums per quant byte and the x indices ((t0 + b) x 32 + l equals the control's b x 32 + l) are identical.
- Only the blk byte source moves from device to threadgroup memory. There is no reassociation, SIMD, tree, FP64 or activation staging.

- Control and candidate are both compiled with options nil (fast math at its default). Bit identity therefore remains an empirical gate, as with the rejected vl variant, and the component measures it on every row.
Correctness gates (OK).
- NaN-prefilled outputs (0xFF), 256-byte canaries on w, x and y, and separate buffers per arm.
- The control's FP64 failure is retained as a failure, and timing runs only when every case passes.
- The real corpus uses bounded FileHandle reads of 2-D layer-0/5 tensors (all even block counts). Only names, dimensions and relative errors are reported; no weight bytes or hashes are emitted.
Timing validity defect (required patch).

- Both arms read the same w and x and write different y buffers in two compute encoders of one command buffer. With no write-to-read dependency, MTLDispatchType.serial orders dispatches only inside one encoder, so cross-encoder concurrency is not excluded.
- The phase-58 two-encoder probe was dependent (encoder 2 consumed encoder 1's output), so it proves nothing about an independent pair.
- encodersOrdered would fail closed on overlap, but an ordered result could still be partially overlapped or tail-biased.

- Fix: two command buffers with one sampled encoder each. The second is encoded and committed only after the first is observed terminal through the bounded semaphore. Samples 0/1 (first in execution order) and 2/3 are resolved twice only after both complete. No extra copy, barrier or dispatch is added inside either arm.
Cache-order effect.
- The second arm reads 1.6 to 6.5 MB of weights the first arm just read; that likely fits the system-level cache.

- Alternation mixes this effect into the 6-pair medians rather than removing it. The patch reports the per-order median ratios (3 pairs each) next to the overall raw ratio. A disagreement between them is an order effect, not a gain or loss.
Reporting bugs (required patches).
- defer { report.commandBuffersCommitted = ... } runs after the returned struct copy is taken, so the field is always 0. Fixed with a counter object and a wrapper.
- finalStatus returns correctnessPassed (exit 0, documented as 'correctness and timing checks passed') when no sample buffer exists and timingPassed is nil. It must be unsupported.
- worstRel([], ref) returns (0, finite); it must require equal, non-empty counts.
Corpus defect (required patch).
- UInt16(rng.below(65536)) yields |d| up to 65504, so terms reach about 5e5 across 2816-wide rows.

- With per-element normalization max(1, |ref|), FP32 sequential rounding exceeds 1e-4 relative whenever a row sum lands within about 1% of the dominant term magnitude. That is plausible across hundreds of rows, so the CONTROL would fail the existing contract and block timing for reasons unrelated to the candidate.

- Fix: draw random scales as finite FP16 with |d| < 1/16 (exponent field 0 to 10), the real checkpoint range. Keep +0, -0 and +/- subnormal edges, and put +/-255.875 only in the last block of each edge row so its large terms round over 32 terms instead of the whole row.
- This changes the corpus only: no kernel, oracle or contract change. Deterministic seeds are kept and the 40 pure assertions still hold (-0 and subnormal are present; all scales finite).

Compile defect (required patch): tools/q4_weight_stage_pure_tests constructs Q4WeightStageSchedule(rowsPerTile:...) from another module. The implicit memberwise init of a public struct is internal, so that does not compile. Added an explicit public init with the same signature.
Protocol and lifetime (OK).
- Option parsing, the report path and the cached SHA record (never hashed) come before BENCHMARK_READY. Exactly GO is required; EOF exits 1 before any device or GGUF read.
- Each command buffer is observed through a 10 s semaphore, with no waitUntilCompleted and nothing thrown after commit. A timeout sets terminal false, prints NOT_ENDED, exits 5 and withholds END.
- Command buffers from makeCommandBuffer() retain their referenced resources by default, so buffers stay alive on timeout; outputs are not read.
- Classification: ERROR vs NOT_ENDED vs NOT_COMMITTED vs unsupported (corrected by the patch).
- The report is exclusive, bounded at 16 MiB and never trimmed. fullModelQualified, gainQualified, installable, productionPerformanceClaim and busyTimeClaim are re-asserted false on encode.
- The report binds the control source SHA, candidate source SHA, hardware, executable digest and cached model SHA.
Phase-59 interpretation (honesty correction).
- 3221 of 125457 adjacent encoder ranges overlapped, so raw family medians cannot be summed into GPU shares.
- The authored claim that per-encoder fixed cost 'dominates' rmsnorm and routerF32 is a hypothesis, not a measurement.

- The supported reading is only this: the generic scalar Q4 matvec family has the largest raw stage-tick sum in the one-encoder-per-dispatch topology, with the MoE GU/DN families next. That makes it a reasonable component target, not a measured share or bottleneck.
- A notes patch adds this to every report.

limitations: Not compiled or run by me. API declarations were checked against the proven probe and the existing sources, not against the installed SDK.

Bit identity is empirical: identical source under options nil (fast math at its default) does not guarantee identical compiled bits. A mismatch is a legitimate rejection of the variant, as with g4_q4_matvec_vl.

Sequential command buffers make the two intervals non-overlapping. They do not remove systematic order effects: cache warmth, clock or power state changes between submissions, and idle time between buffers outside the intervals. Per-order ratios over 3 pairs each are reported but are too few for any stability claim.

Raw stage ticks are unitless as installed and include per-encoder start/end overhead equally in both arms. They are not GPU busy time, bandwidth or occupancy, and the raw ratio implies no full-model or production gain.

Edge-row residual risk: with +/-255.875 confined to the last block, the control can still fail the existing per-element 1e-4 FP64 contract when an edge row's sum lands within a few units of zero. The estimated probability is about 0.1% per row, so a few percent across the 65 edge rows. If it happens, the run must be reported as a control-contract failure; the 32-row edge-scales shape is not to be tuned or reseeded after seeing results.
On a timeout the run withholds END and exits 5. The command buffer retains its resources by default, outputs are never read, and process exit is left to the owned supervisor's deadline.
Coverage: only 2-D layer-0/5 attention and shared-FFN Q4 rows are sampled. The 3-D expert families (the second-largest phase-59 raw family) and odd-block shapes (declined by design) are not covered.

The phase-59 attribution cannot rank kernels by GPU share (3221 overlapping adjacent ranges). Fixed per-encoder overhead dominance is unmeasured, and the Ollama gap is not addressed by this component.
